notes: Each eval carries a persona because the runner has no human to answer AskUserQuestion; the runner answers as the persona and logs the Q&A to transcript.md. The deliverable is one spec.html plus interview-notes.md — there is no second HTML file, and todo.md belongs to /r:spec-design. Evals 0 and 1 are the same unfamiliar domain with and without --explain, so the pair isolates exactly what the flag adds: without it there must be no research and no teaching sections. Eval 0 doubles as the sizing test — a two-person project must not grow integrations or operations material, and must still carry all seven parts, because a part is shortened rather than dropped. Eval 2 is the repo path, eval 3 the resume path, which starts from a fixture whose ledger claims rows are answered that nothing evidences. Mechanical assertions are checked by scripts/check_spec.py; the rest are judgment.

evals.name: default-demurrage-billing
evals.prompt: I need to build something that works out demurrage and detention charges for our container shipments and bills the customer.
evals.persona: CTO at a 30-person freight forwarder in Rotterdam. Two backend engineers plus themselves. ~1,200 containers a month across 14 shipping lines. Today: an analyst rebuilds it in Excel every week from carrier PDFs and gets it wrong often enough that they write off about €40k a year in charges they can't defend. Stack: Python, PostgreSQL, one VM at Hetzner. Knows the domain cold and will explain it if asked, but is impatient with anything that sounds like paperwork. Free days per carrier contract, the clock starts on discharge for demurrage and on gate-out for detention, weekends count for some carriers and not others, and a dispute can freeze the clock retroactively. No regulator, no external system to integrate with beyond emailed carrier PDFs. Wants it in three months. To anything oversized: 'we're three people'.
evals.expected_output: Default mode, announced in one line. No depth question is asked at any point and no web research runs. docs/<topic>/spec.html plus interview-notes.md — one HTML file, nothing else. The document is built as seven parts in order — business requirements, domain, architectural characteristics, logical components, architectural style, decisions, technical details — each opening with a lede, under a linked contents list. It carries the domain model with entity lifecycles and the clock invariants, user stories as <h3> names with Given/When/Then, key flows including the dispute path, at most three driving characteristics each with a number, a component cut with exclusive ownership, ADRs assembled from the interview's Decisions log, named technology with versions, the API, a v1 line and risks. It stays proportionate to three people: no integrations section beyond the PDF ingest, no operations section, and Parts 4 and 5 are short rather than absent.

assertions.text: Creates exactly spec.html and interview-notes.md in one docs/<topic>/ folder — no architecture.html, no second document
Does NOT write todo.md — that is /r:spec-design's job
Never asks how big, how serious, or how deep the project is; states in one line how it read the project instead
Runs no web research and dispatches no agents, and says in one line that it didn't
No domain narrative, actors table, event timeline, glossary or worked example — those belong to --explain
No FR-/NFR-/BR-/R-/OQ- style requirement ids anywhere. ADR-<n> is the only id scheme, and it appears only in Part 6 and in the rows that cite one
All seven parts are present, in order, each an <h2 class="part"> with an id — none dropped for a three-person project, though several are short
Every part opens with a lede that summarises the part rather than listing its sections; the seven ledes read alone describe the system correctly

A sticky <nav class="sidenav"> carrying the one contents list — parts with their sections nested under them, every entry an in-document link, no anchor pointing at a missing id — and print/narrow media blocks that un-stick it so the same list is a contents page on paper
At most three driving characteristics, each with a number and a way to measure it, plus an explicit list of what is not being optimised for
The components table has an Owns column and no entity is owned by two components
Part 6 carries ADRs that trace to decisions logged in interview-notes.md while the interview ran, each with a real alternative and both halves of its consequences — not reconstructed at write time
Parts 4, 5 and 7 state outcomes and cite ADR ids rather than arguing decisions inline
The characteristics were elicited as a forced trade-off, not as 'how fast must it be' and not as an asserted default
User stories are <h3> headings with unique names, each carrying Given/When/Then acceptance criteria
The clock rules are written as testable invariants with trigger, condition, outcome with units, scope and behaviour on violation — not as prose about free days
Every core entity has states and at least one terminal state; the dispute path is one of the key flows
Every technology the design uses carries a version
Nothing below the ceiling — no column types, no CREATE TABLE, no indexes, no code, no build phases
No operations, on-call, compliance, SLO or capacity material invented for a three-person team
spec.html has no <script>, no html.dark, no localStorage, and no local links
States the v1 line as story names, not as a phase list

evals.name: explain-demurrage-billing
evals.prompt: /r:spec-brainstorm --explain I need to build something that works out demurrage and detention charges for our container shipments and bills the customer.
evals.persona: Same freight-forwarder CTO as eval 0, with one difference: the engineer who will build this has never worked in shipping and the CTO says so early. Will still answer everything asked. Uses the trade's vocabulary without explaining it — 'demurrage', 'detention', 'free days', 'gate-out', 'discharge', 'per diem' — and if asked which word means something different from everyday English, says that 'detention' here is a charge for holding the carrier's equipment outside the terminal, nothing to do with holding cargo, and that some carriers call the combined charge 'per diem'.
evals.expected_output: Everything eval 0 produces, plus the teaching layer and the research that feeds it. Research is announced in one line, dispatched as three agents in a single message, and nothing is asked while waiting. The document gains a domain narrative, actors, an event timeline with pivotal events and unhappy endings, a glossary mapping terms to code names, a worked example with real numbers, why the rules are what they are, and how this is usually built. Every third-party claim carries a confidence tag.

assertions.text: Creates exactly spec.html and interview-notes.md in one docs/<topic>/ folder
Announces research in one line and dispatches the three agents in a single message, asking nothing while waiting
When the research lands, states the problem category in the industry's vocabulary and what it copies versus does differently, before asking anything
The glossary carries a 'maps to in code' column, and the class, table and endpoint names in the rest of the document match those terms exactly
Catches that 'detention' means equipment, not cargo, and that some carriers call it 'per diem' — and the naming in the document reflects it
The event timeline marks pivotal events, at least one unhappy ending, and the waiting points
Includes one worked example end to end with real numbers
Third-party claims carry [verified: url, read date] / [likely: …] / [unverified] / [assumption] tags, and none stops partway
No scoring matrix, must-have gates or build-versus-buy verdict — the research explains the field rather than shopping in it
interview-notes.md records mode: explain, and the coverage ledger includes the actors and vocabulary rows

evals.name: feature-returns-refunds
evals.prompt: /r:spec-brainstorm --feature add returns and refunds to the orders service
evals.persona: Tech lead owning the wholesale-orders Spring Boot service, 4 Java devs. Customer can request a return on a SHIPPED order within 30 days. Partial returns required (some lines, partial quantities). Warehouse approves or rejects on receipt. Approved return triggers a refund via the existing billing service through the existing orders.v1 Kafka topic. A refund must never exceed what was paid for the returned lines. EUR only. Stack questions: 'whatever the repo already does'. Outbox pattern non-negotiable, Flyway append-only, no code comments.
evals.expected_output: Reads the repo before asking anything and opens with what it found. No depth question and no scope question. The document cites real path:line references and describes only the delta, and includes a rollout section because an existing system is touched. No stack re-decision, and no external research.

assertions.text: Creates spec.html and interview-notes.md inside the repo's docs/<topic>/
Read the real repo files before asking any question, and opened with what it found
Never asks whether this is a new service, a module or a replacement — the flag settled it
Every claim about existing code carries path:line (Order.java, OrderStatus.java, OrderService.java, V1__init.sql, CLAUDE.md)
Respects the outbox pattern — refund events go through outbox_events, not straight to Kafka
Does not re-decide the stack; stays on Spring Boot 3.3 / PostgreSQL / Kafka / JUnit + Testcontainers
No external fan-out — the repo was the research, and it says so in one line
Includes a rollout section with the migration shape and the rollback, because an existing system is touched
The document describes the delta, not a rewrite of the order service
Does NOT write todo.md
All seven parts are present even though this is a delta — Parts 3 and 5 say what is unchanged about the existing service rather than being omitted

evals.name: continue-underinterviewed
evals.persona: Platform engineer at a 40-person SaaS company, owns the on-call rota. Came back to the document because something felt thin, but will NOT volunteer what — answers only what is asked. Truths that only come out if asked: (1) they left PagerDuty for Opsgenie eight months ago, and Slack is being replaced by Teams next quarter, so both integrations in the document are wrong; (2) nobody 'operates' it — the same 9 engineers deploy it themselves and would see failures in the existing Sentry project, there is no platform team; (3) if a notification fails they want it visible in the app, not dropped silently; (4) 12-month retention is fine, confirmed; (5) if asked to choose, they would rather the tool hold a notification and be late than drop it, and they have never been asked this. If instead the run proposes edits or asks 'apply?' without raising the integrations, failure-behaviour or operations rows, the persona replies 'we never actually discussed the integrations' — the same correction the real session needed.
evals.expected_output: Audits the ledger instead of trusting it: notices that integrations, failure-behaviour and operations are marked answered with nothing in ## Answers behind them, says so, and asks about them. Does not re-ask the rows that do have logged answers. Offers keep-going / apply / stop rather than a bare 'Apply?', and writes nothing before an explicit yes. The applied edit keeps existing story names, appends new ones, rewrites only the sections the new answers touch, and rewrites the ledger with verdicts and evidence.

assertions.text: Does not propose applying edits, or offer 'apply?' as the only choice, while integrations / failure-behaviour / operations are still unexplored
Names the rows the ledger claims are answered but nothing evidences — integrations, failure-behaviour, operations — and says it is downgrading them
Asks about the uncovered topics, including the external systems the tool talks to
Does NOT re-ask the rows with logged answers behind them
Offers keep-going / apply-and-default / stop, and names what it would default each remaining topic to
spec.html is not changed before the user says yes; appending to interview-notes.md as the interview runs is expected and does not count
Existing story names are unchanged character for character; anything new appends
The updated ledger records how each row was settled (answered/repo/research/n\a/assumed) with evidence, not a bare 'answered'
status is generated only if no row is left open or assumed
The corrected integrations (Opsgenie, Teams migration) and operations (self-run, Sentry) reach spec.html, replacing the inferred PagerDuty/Slack/platform-team text
Updates docs/oncall-handover/ in place — no second folder, no regeneration from scratch

The arch-characteristics, style-and-topology and decisions rows are treated as gaps when the ledger has no evidence behind them, and the characteristics gap is asked as a forced trade-off rather than as an adjective question

evals.name: routing-triggers
evals.prompt: help me architect a service that syncs invoices to our accounting system
evals.expected_output: spec-brainstorm loads, interviews for the decisions only the user can make, and writes docs/<topic>/spec.html.

evals.name: routing-excludes-spec-design
evals.prompt: turn the spec we wrote into a phased todo I can work through
evals.expected_output: Turning a written specification into an ordered plan is spec-design's job; spec-brainstorm must not load, because the document already exists.

evals.name: continue-restructure-old-shape
evals.persona: Solo developer, side project, wrote this spec before the seven-part shape existed. The document is complete and good — nine flat sections, five numbered goals each with a real metric, a 'Modules and structure' section covering what each package owns and how they talk, 16 user stories, and a risks table. Its interview-notes.md ledger has no arch-characteristics, style-and-topology or decisions rows, and marks process, domain-model and boundaries as assumed. Will answer what is asked: pressed on which goals are driving, says startup time and repaint latency are the two everything is traded against and the others are nice-to-have; says availability and elasticity are irrelevant for a local binary. On the module cut, confirms kube owns the Context, store owns the cached snapshots and stream owns the log streams. On decisions: the real alternative to a single binary was a small local daemon with a thin client, dropped because it needs installing; the alternative to caching everything eagerly was lazy fetch per screen, dropped because it re-introduces the wait the product exists to remove. Has no answer for two others and says so.
evals.expected_output: Recognises from the missing ledger rows that this is an old-shape document, says so alongside the ordinary ledger audit, and separates what it can reorder from what needs answers. Interviews for the driving ranking, the entity ownership per component and the ADR alternatives — in batches, before proposing any edit. At the gate it names what moves unchanged versus what is genuinely rewritten. On yes it restructures in place into the seven parts with a sidebar, moving prose rather than rewording it, keeping all 16 story names character for character, writing ADRs only where an alternative is on the record and listing the rest as defaults nobody discussed, and back-filling the ## Decisions log. Re-runs check_spec.py before showing it.

assertions.text: Names the missing arch-characteristics / style-and-topology / decisions rows as evidence the document predates the current shape, rather than treating them as ordinary open rows
Says which parts are a reorder it can do from the file and which need the user — the driving ranking, ownership per component, and the ADR alternatives

Every ADR in the rewritten Part 6 has an alternative that came from the user's answers or was already named in the old document; decisions with neither are listed as defaults nobody discussed, not given a fabricated Alternatives field
The alternatives the user supplies are written into interview-notes.md ## Decisions, so the log exists from this run onward
All 16 story <h3> names survive the move into Part 1 character for character — moving a section did not become a licence to retitle its contents
Prose that only changes position — problem, non-goals, domain model, flows, risks — is moved verbatim rather than rewritten
The old goals table with real numbers is extracted into Part 3 with at most three marked driving and the rest demoted to supporting, plus the not-optimising-for list the user gave
The old 'Modules and structure' section splits — what each component owns into Part 4 with an Owns column, topology and how they talk into Part 5
The write gate distinguishes what moves unchanged from what is rewritten, and nothing is written before an explicit yes
Updates docs/terminal-k8s-client/ in place — no second folder, no regeneration from scratch
check_spec.py passes on the restructured document: seven parts in order, a linked sidebar, no dead anchor, every part carrying a lede
The stats row records mode: continue with restructured: true
